rows.note: In Q 103:1 al-ʿaṣr means passing time or age, often the afternoon, while biblical עצר means restrain or hold back and extends to rule and solemn assembly.

rows.explanation: עֲצָרַנִי means “restrained me from bearing,” a withholding sense absent from al-ʿaṣr’s temporal use.
עָצֹר עָצַר says the LORD had “closed up” the wombs, using עצר for restraint rather than time.
וְעָצַר אֶת־הַשָּׁמַיִם means “he shut up the heaven,” a restraining sense unlike al-ʿaṣr.
וַתֵּעָצַר הַמַּגֵּפָה says the plague was stopped, using עצר for cessation.
וַתֵּעָצַר הַמַּגֵּפָה again says the plague was stayed, a stopping sense rather than a time period.
עָצְרוּ בַבָּיִת says the cows’ calves were kept shut up at home, a restraining sense.
נֶעְצָר לִפְנֵי יְהוָה describes Doeg as detained before the LORD, not as being in a particular period of time.
אַל־תַּעֲצָר־לִי means “slack not” or “do not stop” the ride, using עצר for holding back.
יַעְצֹר בַּמַּיִם means God “withholds the waters,” a restraining sense unlike al-ʿaṣr.
וְעָצַרְתִּי asks whether God would “shut the womb,” using עצר for restraint.
עֹצֶר רָחַם is the “barren womb,” literally a closed or restrained womb rather than a time.
יַעְצֹר בְּעַמִּי is rendered “shall reign over my people,” extending the root’s sense of holding in check to rule.
עָצוּר וְעָזוּב, “shut up and left,” is a paired expression for those confined and those remaining.
עָצוּר וְעָזוּב repeats the paired expression “shut up and left.”
עָצוּר וְעָזוּב בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל repeats the expression for those shut up and those left in Israel.
עָצוּר וְעָזוּב בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל repeats the same “shut up and left” expression.
אֶפֶס עָצוּר וְאֶפֶס עָזוּב repeats the paired expression, “none shut up and none left.”
עֲצֶרֶת is a holy assembly, a gathering sense distinct from al-ʿaṣr’s meaning of time.
עֲצֶרֶת names the solemn assembly on the eighth day, not a period of time.
עֲצֶרֶת names the solemn assembly on the seventh day, a gathering sense.
עֲצָרָה is a solemn assembly proclaimed for Baal, not a time word.
עֲצָרָה means a solemn meeting, a gathering rather than a period.
עֲצָרֹת means solemn assemblies, a gathering sense unlike al-ʿaṣr.
עֲצָרָה is a solemn assembly called with a fast, not a time period.
קִרְאוּ עֲצָרָה means “call a solemn assembly,” using the root for a gathering.
עֲצֶרֶת is the solemn assembly held on the eighth day, a gathering sense.
עֲצֶרֶת is the solemn assembly held on the eighth day, not a word for time.
